title: Mix every unknown uniformly SPD medium using scalar-baseline energy comparison
statement: For arbitrary measurable lambda I<=a(t,x)<=Lambda I, compare its weak divergence-form evolution U_a with the same-field scalar S_lambda over a window tau. For unit initial f, the energy identity gives ||U_a f-S_lambda f||2^2<=K0^2 D, D=1-||U_a f||2^2,K0=(Lambda-lambda)/(sqrt(2)lambda). Baseline operator norm<=1/4 then forces D>=1/[16(1+K0)^2]. Choose k=ceil[64(1+Lambda/lambda)^2/epsilon],tau=t/k and one scalar field with that window contraction; uniform repeated contraction yields ||U_a(t,0)||mean-zero L2-to-L2<=epsilon for ALL such unknown media. Baseline construction at these numerical parameters preserves a fixed polynomial resource bound. This uses the weak energy identity, not operator/semigroup monotonicity, and needs neither coefficient derivative bounds nor access to a itself.
